title: Split geometric projection: derived adjunction and diagonal unit
statement:
Fix $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Use the rationalized and common-stage constructible categories and hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart], and the derived inverse and direct images [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $h:Y\to X$ a morphism with a specified finite nonempty clopen decomposition $Y=\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i$ and isomorphisms $s_i:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_i$ satisfying $h s_i=\operatorname{id}_X$.
Under the coefficient-compatible clopen equivalence [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition], the actual derived adjunction $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions] identifies with the diagonal/product adjunction:
$$Lh^*K\longleftrightarrow(K)_{i\in I},\qquad Rh_*H\simeq\prod_{i\in I}s_i^*(H|_{Y_i}).$$
These are identifications in the derived categories, natural in $K,H$ and compatible with finite coefficient extension. On constructible hearts the finite product is the biproduct. The Hom bijection sends a tuple $(u_i:K\to s_i^*(H|_{Y_i}))_i$ to the map to the product with components $u_i$; the unit on $K$ is the diagonal and the counit on each sheet is the corresponding projection.
In particular, for $M$ in the heart there is a canonical identification $h_*h^*M\simeq\bigoplus_{i\in I}M$. The morphism $T_M:h_*h^*M\to M$ whose restriction to each summand is $\operatorname{id}_M$ has geometric-stalk map $(v_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i v_i$, and $T_M\eta_M=|I|\operatorname{id}_M$. These assertions hold also for $X=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Write $j_i:Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$ and $a_i=j_i s_i:X\to Y$, so $h a_i=\mathrm{id}_X$. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $h^{-1}U=\coprod_iU=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_i A)$. This algebra is a finite free $A$-module, generated as an algebra by its finitely many coordinate idempotents. Thus $h$ is finite and finite type. In $Y\times_XY=\coprod_{i,j}X$, its diagonal is the identity on diagonal pairs and empty on off-diagonal pairs, hence is closed. Thus $h$ is separated. Also $Y$ is finite type over $k$ as a finite union of copies of $X$. Its absolute diagonal is the closed diagonal of $X$ on diagonal pairs in $\coprod_{i,j}(X\times_kX)$, and empty otherwise, so $Y$ is separated over $k$. The adjunction and clopen-comparison hypotheses hold, also for empty $X$.

source.place: Paragraph 5: split finite etale projection; affine verification of the hypotheses

proof.text: Put $\Phi H=(Ls_i^*Lj_i^*H)_i$. On integral constructible objects open restriction to $Y_i$ is naturally isomorphic to $Lj_i^*$ [lem-pur-open-completed-restriction-identification], and $Ls_i^*\cong s_i^{-1}$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], an exact equivalence [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. So at each finite coefficient field $\Phi$ is isomorphic to the equivalence of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] followed by these sheet equivalences, hence an equivalence. At $\Qlb$, Hom sets are colimits over common stages; $\Phi$ gives stagewise bijections compatible with stage transitions, as the comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] are natural and tower-compatible; so $\Phi$ is an equivalence. These isomorphisms serve only this equivalence property. Its cohomology is componentwise. At finite coefficients, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies $La_i^*Lh^*$ with $L(h a_i)^*$; at integral coefficients this is [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], applied also to $s_i,j_i$. For the identity morphism, identify this last functor with the identity using the inverse of the SPECIFIED comparison $\kappa^{\mathrm{id}}$, invertible on complete objects by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. This chooses the normalized comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism $L\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$. This gives a natural comparison $\alpha:\Phi Lh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta$, where $\Delta K=(K)_i$. Rationalize these integral comparisons on Hom groups, and use representatives at a common finite field for $\Qlb$, exactly as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Coefficient coherence of these specified comparisons is checked in step 6.

proof.text:
Put $H_i=(\Phi H)_i$ and $R_H=Rh_*H$. Full faithfulness of $\Phi$, $\alpha$, and the actual Hom bijection of [fix-prop-adjunctions] give natural bijections
$$b_{K,H}:\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(K,H_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_H).$$
Explicitly, regard $(u_i)$ as $\Delta K\to\Phi H$, precompose with $\alpha_K$, lift through the fully faithful $\Phi$, and take its actual $h$-adjunct. Define $p_i:R_H\to H_i$ by $(p_i)_i=b_{R_H,H}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_{R_H})$. Naturality in $K$ gives $p_i b_{K,H}(u)=u_i$. Hence $(R_H,(p_i))$ is a product cone: existence of its map from $K$ is $b_{K,H}(u)$ and uniqueness is injectivity of $b$. This constructs the derived product without an assumption about products in a heart or any passage through stalks. Naturality in $H$ follows from naturality of $b$. The comparison with any chosen product is the unique isomorphism preserving every projection, since the two maps supplied by the product properties compose to identities.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following discussion; explicit product universal-property calculation

proof.text: The actual unit is the adjunct of $\mathrm{id}_{Lh^*K}$. Transporting the latter by $\alpha$ gives $(\mathrm{id}_K)_i$, so $p_i\eta_K=\mathrm{id}_K$ for every $i$: the unit is the diagonal. The actual counit at $H$ is the inverse adjunct of $\mathrm{id}_{R_H}$. By the definition of $p_i$ in step 3 its $i$-th component is $p_i$. Thus the comparison identifies the prescribed adjunction, including its Hom bijection, unit and counit, rather than only its two functors.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint: unit and counit as the identity transposes

proof.text: Finite products here are biproducts. In the additive derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define $\iota_i:H_i\to P=\prod_jH_j$ by $p_j\iota_i=\delta_{ji}\mathrm{id}$ (zero when $j\ne i$). Projectionwise verification gives $\sum_i\iota_i p_i=\mathrm{id}_P$. Therefore $\sum_i f_i p_i:P\to N$ is the unique map whose composites with the $\iota_i$ are prescribed maps $f_i:H_i\to N$. This proves the coproduct property. If the $H_i$ lie in the standard constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], their finite biproduct lies there: its cohomology outside degree zero is the finite sum of zero cohomology objects. Thus the product comparison restricts to the hearts. In particular $h_*h^*M=\bigoplus_iM$ with the diagonal unit of step 4.

source.place: Tag 0037 and finite additive product calculation; standard cohomology computed on finite direct sums of complexes

proof.text: The comparison $\alpha$ uses the specified integral composition comparisons and the identity-isomorphism pullback comparison, not independent choices at each coefficient field. Their compatibility with $E\subset L$ is [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension], clause 1, and [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension] applied to the identity isomorphism. The functor $\Phi=(Ls_i^*Lj_i^*)_i$ commutes with scalar extension through the natural comparisons $\alpha^{j_i},\alpha^{s_i}$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; by naturality, lifting a morphism through the fully faithful $\Phi$ commutes with scalar extension. Finally [lem-pur-ordinary-adjunction-scalar-compatibility] says that the actual ordinary Hom bijections and their inverses commute with these coefficient comparisons, after rationalization and on common-stage representatives. Applying these equalities to the explicit construction of $b$ in step 3 proves coefficient compatibility of $b$ and of every $p_i$. Thus the product comparison, its unit and counit, and the biproduct injections characterized by $p_j\iota_i=\delta_{ji}$ all commute with finite coefficient extension. The same equalities at a common finite field make all constructions independent of the representative at $\Qlb$.

source.place: Paragraph 5: diagonal and summation, expanded using the specified coefficient-comparison statements

proof.text:
For the repeated family $M$, define $T_M=\sum_i p_i:\bigoplus_iM\to M$. Then $T_M\iota_j=\mathrm{id}_M$ and uniqueness follows from the coproduct property. Also
$$T_M\eta_M=\sum_i p_i\eta_M=\sum_i\mathrm{id}_M=|I|\mathrm{id}_M.$$
At any geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, its stalk operation on morphisms is additive: for module sheaves, addition of germs is addition after a common pointed refinement [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], so $(f+g)_{\bar x}=f_{\bar x}+g_{\bar x}$. Applying this termwise to complexes, then taking cohomology or the compatible integral coefficient towers, preserves the same addition equation. Raw rationalization and common finite stages extend this equation linearly. For $\Omega=k$ the point-evaluation model is explicitly [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with the linear coefficient formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Applying the additive stalk operation to the equations for $p_i,\iota_i$ preserves their finite biproduct equations, and sends $T_M$ to $\sum_i(p_i)_{\bar x}$. Hence its stalk map is exactly $(v_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i v_i$. For $X=\varnothing$, every $Y_i$ and $Y$ is empty. The empty-cover clause of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] makes these derived categories zero categories. All comparisons and equations above are then the unique morphisms, and the stalk assertion has no points to test. For $|I|=1$ the same formulas give identity unit and summation.
